notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left. Foreign white plates are fairly common in this small country.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black and white wedge bollards with grey reflectors, some with an indent in the lower half. Reflectors have three bolts, not the two seen next door to the east.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows, rarely blue and yellow; none of the neighbours use them.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are yellow with a thin black outline, uppercase names, a pointed tip and a full frame around them.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Regional road numbers have 1 or 2 digits in a red box; local ones have 3 digits in a yellow box.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Yellow framed town entrance signs, usually showing the name in two languages, often with road number and speed limit on top.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Frames around road signs have square corners; Denmark uses similar but more rounded ones.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Almost all road signs are mounted on white posts, also seen less commonly in France.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs are short and usually white, often with slanted blue corners. Belgian ones can be other colours; Dutch ones are long and blue.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs have 5 vertical stripes; Belgium's has 2 horizontal ones.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Blue bus stop signs always use one design: a bus with six windows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Some signposts carry a bulky round reflector with blue and white markings, as in Sweden and Finland.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: The commonest pole top looks like an upside-down trident; these also occur in France, Spain and Portugal.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Three official languages: signs and ads are mostly in the Romance one, less often the Germanic one; the local tongue has umlauts and double vowels.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Green rolling hills with a patchwork of farmland and forest. Unlike the flat yellow-plated Netherlands.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Dark slate roofs and plain undecorated walls in white, grey or pastel; similar nearby in Belgium and France.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Nearly all coverage is Generation 2 or 4; Generation 3 is rare.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Three-digit local roads: 1xx in the southern half, 2xx around the capital, 3xx in the northern half.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north is hillier and higher than the south.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Vineyards are mostly found in the southeast.
